fields.subnational_unit: national (Uganda); respondents from KCCA, NWSC and the Ministry of Water and Environment, NGOs and a private firm
fields.population: professionals in water and sanitation organisations in Uganda (government, NGO, private) and national aid and coverage data 2015-2022
fields.sample_size: 10 purposively sampled professionals (6 men, 4 women) from KCCA, NWSC, Ministry of Water and Environment, Water for People, Green Empowerment, Technology for Tomorrow, UNICEF and WaterAid; secondary national data on official development assistance and JMP coverage, 2015-2022
fields.effect_measure: convergent mixed methods: thematic analysis of 10 respondent accounts and descriptive trend analysis of aid inflows against percentage coverage of basic water and sanitation (SDG 6.1 and 6.2)
fields.effect_estimate: As official development assistance to the sector rose, the share of the population with at least basic drinking water rose; basic sanitation coverage stayed stagnant; rural-urban inequalities persist. Aid-funded projects show functionality problems, short-term success and poor sustainability attributed to weak local involvement; the sector is highly dependent on external finance. Association from descriptive trends only; no inferential statistics or coefficients.
fields.model_type: thematic analysis plus descriptive trend analysis of secondary data
fields.study_design: convergent mixed-methods single-country case study (Master's thesis): purposive expert respondents and national time-series data
fields.section: Full text (Master's thesis, Webster University Leiden): Abstract; Chapter III methodology; results (partly)
fields.exact_location: Abstract p iv-v; Chapter III 3.1-3.2 p30-33 (design, sampling, Table 1); results chapters
fields.table: Table 1 (respondents); coverage and aid tables not read

risk_of_bias_rating: CASP Qualitative per-item (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28): 1(aims)=Yes; 2(qual approach)=Yes; 3(design)=Yes (convergent mixed design explained); 4(recruitment)=Can't tell (purposive selection described; recruitment process and refusals not given); 5(data collection)=Can't tell (respondent data collection method not seen in the part read); 6(researcher-participant)=Can't tell; 7(ethics)=Can't tell; 8(analysis rigor)=Can't tell (thematic and trend analysis described briefly); 9(findings)=Yes; 10(value)=Yes. Per CASP's own guidance no composite score is computed.
evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a Master's thesis (convergent mixed methods; 10 expert respondents and 2015-2022 national aid and coverage trends) on foreign aid and SDG 6 progress in Uganda, read in full text 2026-10-04 (abstract and methods; results partly). Rising aid coincides with rising basic-water coverage but flat sanitation; sustainability and dependency problems. Descriptive; the exposure is aid finance, not a legal or administrative rule.
